en.name: Cooked octopus
en.summary: Cooked octopus — boiled tender for pulpo a feira, salads and tapas — keeps 3–4 days in the fridge and 1–3 months in the freezer. The critical step is cooling it fast: a whole octopus left in its pot stays warm for hours.
en.pantry: Cooked seafood must never be left out of the refrigerator for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F). Octopus is the classic offender, because a large one holds heat like a stone: left in the cooking water it drifts down through the danger zone between 4 and 60 °C for a long time. Pull the tentacles out of the hot water, spread them on a tray so they cool quickly, and refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.
en.fridge: Keep cooked octopus at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use it within 3–4 days, which is the published figure for cooked fish and shellfish. Storing it under a little of its own cooking liquor stops it drying and keeps the skin intact, but it does not extend the window. Slice it only when you are ready to serve — sliced rounds dry at the edges and lose the gloss that makes the dish. Cooked octopus sold vacuum-packed in the chiller carries its own use-by date and is usually pasteurised, so it keeps longer than a home-boiled one; once that pack is opened, this record applies.
en.freezer: Cooked octopus keeps 1–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze the tentacles whole rather than sliced, with a splash of the cooking liquor, bagged flat with the air pressed out. Freezing raw octopus before cooking is the old trick for tenderness — the ice crystals break down the muscle — and it genuinely works, so buying it frozen is no loss at all. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight, never on the counter, and use it within a day or two. Warm slices gently in a little liquor or olive oil rather than boiling them again, which toughens them. Do not refreeze.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell instead of a clean, sweet-briny one.
A slimy or sticky surface on the tentacles.
Skin that has gone grey and is sloughing off in patches.
Cloudy, ropy liquor in the container, or a fizzy taste.
tips: Spread the tentacles on a tray to cool, never leave them in the pot.
Store under a little cooking liquor, and slice only at serving time.
Freeze tentacles whole; sliced rounds lose texture.
Buying frozen raw octopus is an advantage, not a compromise — it cooks more tender.

faq.q: How long does cooked octopus keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 3–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, ideally under a little of its cooking liquor.
Yes, 1–3 months at −18 °C. Freeze the tentacles whole with a splash of liquor rather than slicing them first.

faq.q: Does freezing octopus make it more tender?
faq.a: Yes. Ice crystals break down the dense muscle, which is why frozen raw octopus often cooks more tender than fresh.

faq.q: How should you cool a whole cooked octopus?
faq.a: Lift it out of the hot water and spread the tentacles on a tray, then refrigerate within 2 hours. Left in the pot it stays warm for hours.

zh.name: 熟章魚
zh.summary: 熟章魚——也就是煮到軟嫩、拿來做西班牙加利西亞章魚、沙拉和小菜的那種——冷藏可放 3～4 天，冷凍 1～3 個月。關鍵步驟是快速降溫：整隻章魚留在鍋裡會溫好幾個小時。
zh.pantry: 熟海鮮離開冷藏不得超過 2 小時，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。章魚是最典型的例子，因為大隻的章魚像石頭一樣蓄熱：留在煮汁裡，它會在 4 到 60 °C 的危險溫度帶裡慢慢往下降很久。請把腳撈出來攤在盤上快速降溫，並在煮好後 2 小時內冰起來。
zh.fridge: 熟章魚放 4 °C 以下，3～4 天內用完，這是「熟魚與熟貝甲類」的公告值。加一點自己的煮汁蓋著可以防止乾掉、也保住表皮，但不會延長期限。要上桌時才切片——切好的章魚片邊緣會乾掉，也失去那層讓菜好看的光澤。冷藏櫃裡真空包裝的熟章魚有自己的有效日期、通常也經過殺菌，所以比家裡煮的耐放；但那包一開，就適用本篇的規則。
zh.freezer: 熟章魚在 −18 °C 下可放 1～3 個月。請整隻腳冷凍、不要先切片，加一點煮汁，壓平裝袋並擠出空氣。「煮之前先冷凍生章魚」是讓它變嫩的老方法——冰晶會破壞肌肉纖維——而且真的有效，所以買冷凍章魚完全不吃虧。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍，不要放室溫，解凍後一兩天內用完。切片要回溫的話，用一點煮汁或橄欖油溫熱即可，不要再煮沸，那會讓它變硬。不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨的鹹甜海味。
外皮轉灰並一塊塊剝落。
容器裡的汁液混濁牽絲，或吃起來有氣泡感。
tips: 把腳攤在盤上降溫，絕對不要留在鍋裡。
加一點煮汁蓋著保存，上桌前才切片。
整隻腳冷凍；切好的片會失去口感。
買冷凍生章魚是優勢而不是妥協——煮起來更嫩。

faq.q: 熟章魚冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下 3～4 天，最好加一點煮汁蓋著。
可以，−18 °C 下 1～3 個月。整隻腳連一點煮汁冷凍，不要先切片。

faq.q: 冷凍過的章魚比較嫩嗎？
faq.a: 是的。冰晶會破壞緻密的肌肉，所以冷凍生章魚煮起來常常比生鮮的更嫩。

faq.q: 整隻煮好的章魚要怎麼降溫？
faq.a: 從熱湯裡撈出來、把腳攤在盤上，並在 2 小時內冰起來。留在鍋裡它會溫好幾個小時。
